name: dev-guard
description: A simple security auditor for VS Code-compatible IDE extensions that checks for known malicious extensions.
author: v0ldemort5545-unsafe_call

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Dev-Guard scans .vscode/ files and extensions in Restricted Mode before a folder is trusted.

commands.title: Dev-Guard: Scan Workspace & Profile for File Threats
Extension Security Auditor: Check Installed Extensions

devGuard.telemetry.enabled.description: Send pseudonymous usage statistics to pkgscan.dev. When a malicious extension is found, its ID and installed version are included. No file paths are collected. Respects VS Code's global telemetry setting.

enumDescriptions: Automatically uninstall extensions flagged as malicious and show a summary notification with a Reload Window action.
Show one batched notification with an Uninstall button when malicious extensions are found.
Show a warning notification only; never uninstall automatically.
devGuard.removalMode.description: How dev-guard responds when an installed extension matches a malicious advisory from the pkgscan.dev advisories feed.

devGuard.marketplace.markdownDescription: Marketplace gallery URL to match advisories against. Leave **empty** to detect it from the editor's `product.json` (default). Enter a custom URL such as `https://open-vsx.org/vscode/gallery` if your editor uses a different gallery. Known hosts map to VS Code Marketplace, Cursor Marketplace, or Open VSX; unknown hosts are checked against every marketplace. Sideloaded `.vsix` extensions are always checked against every marketplace.

devGuard.proxy.enabled.description: Run a lightweight local marketplace proxy on 127.0.0.1 that injects pkgscan.dev scan summaries at the top of extension READMEs and blocks downloads of extensions with security advisories. Updates the configured marketplace to the local proxy when enabled and restores your previous marketplace when turned off.

devGuard.allowlist.description: Extension IDs (publisher.name) that dev-guard must never flag or uninstall, even if they match a malicious advisory. In auto mode a flagged extension is removed again every time it is reinstalled until its ID is listed here.

devGuard.allowedFiles.description: Files dev-guard should not flag. Each entry is the file name with its SHA-256 in parentheses, such as .vscode/tasks.json (abc123...). A bare hash is still accepted.

devGuard.historyLimit.markdownDescription: How many entries to keep in the DevGuard pane's **Scan log** and **Audit log**. Oldest entries are dropped first. Background scans run about every 5 minutes, so `200` is roughly a day of scan history. Applies immediately.
